subject: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC - next steps

Subject: POC recap + next steps (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)

Hi Liam / Priya —

Great to meet you both today — thanks for the productive demo and the context on your evaluation goals. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get the POC scheduled: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Success criteria you called out: (1) latency under 150ms 95th percentile for short-chat flows, (2) embeddings recall >= 0.85 on your relevance test set, (3) token cost target <$0.003/token during evaluation, (4) end-to-end security review (S3 access patterns + audit logs).
- Workloads: mixed chat + reranking + batch embedding jobs (~10k embeddings/day).
- Data sensitivity: several fields considered regulated; you prefer not to send PHI outside your VPC for the final acceptance tests.

Environment options (high level):
1) Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted API with strict tenant isolation and token-level logging. Quick to start (1-2 business days), good for feature & quality evaluation.
2) Dedicated sandbox: reserved GPU pool in our hosted environment; predictable throughput and capacity for load testing. Setup 3-7 business days depending on sizing.
3) VPC/private deployment: customer VPC or private plane (best for regulatory/data residency). Longer lead time (2-4 weeks) for network & KMS setup.

Recommended path: start with a short hosted trial to validate model & prompts end-to-end, then move to a short dedicated sandbox or VPC for final performance and security acceptance. This keeps time-to-first-result low while preserving an upgrade path.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: 95th pct <150ms for chat flows
- Embedding recall: >=0.85 on provided eval set
- Cost: unit token cost < $0.003 during POC
- Security: access pattern doc + one SOC-2 evidence checklist item completed

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa (me): schedule kickoff + map mutual action plan (MAP) and share MOP + network diagram (attached).
- Dev (cc): technical lead for onboarding, will scope firewall/IP/KMS requirements.
- Acme (Liam): confirm success criteria and preferred environment (hosted / dedicated / VPC) and provide contact for network engineer if VPC.

Attachments: redwood-poc-mop.pdf (outline of MAP), network-diagram.png (example topology).

Can you confirm the success criteria above and which environment you prefer to start with? If hosted works, I can get a sandbox provisioned by Monday. If you want VPC we'll start the network checklist and propose a kickoff next week.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Security/data residency: for the initial eval we can avoid PHI, but our security team will want to run the acceptance tests inside our VPC for final sign-off. So we expect to need VPC option for the last phase.
- Network: we use S3 with cross-account roles; if we do VPC, we'll need either VPC peering or PrivateLink-style connectivity and KMS integration (we use AWS KMS).
- Timing: we'd like to start light this month if possible. If hosted can be ready in a couple days and we can validate quality, that would be ideal. But we need a clear path to VPC within 2-3 weeks for final tests.

Could you send the VPC network checklist and an estimated timeline for a VPC setup? I'll loop in our network engineer (cc'ed Priya) once we have the checklist.

—Liam

Hi Liam / Priya —

Quick technical note on the options and what we'll need if you pick VPC: 

Hosted trial (fastest)
- Pros: <48 hours to provision, no network changes, includes token-level cost/latency dashboards. Good for prompt engineering and quality checks.
- Cons: not suitable for regulated acceptance tests requiring customer-controlled keys.

Dedicated sandbox
- Pros: reserved capacity, better throughput for load tests, isolated pool.
- Lead time: typically 3-7 business days depending on GPU queue and region.

VPC / Private deployment
- Pros: customer-controlled networking, KMS/HSM integration, full audit log separation.
- Lead time: 10-20 business days typical (depends on security review & network engineer availability).

VPC checklist (summary):
- IP allowlist / peering details or PrivateLink endpoint requirements
- Egress/ingress ports (we'll provide a minimal set)
- Cross-account IAM role for S3 access (if you prefer us to read training data) or signed URLs
- KMS key ARN + access policy or customer-managed envelope keys
- Certificate + TLS expectations for PrivateLink
If you want, I can attach the full network checklist (detailed). For a short timeline: start hosted immediately to validate quality; as you said, we can prepare the VPC checklist and start network conversations in parallel — we can target VPC readiness in ~2 weeks if your network team is available.

Proposed dates:
- Hosted trial provisioning: Monday 13 Jul 2026 (if you sign off today)
- VPC kickoff: Wed 15 Jul 2026 (network contact + scoping)
- VPC readiness target: 27 Jul 2026 (target)
Happy to jump on a 30-min tech kickoff with your network engineer — propose Wed 15 Jul 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
